reading.body:
James Green's AI lobbying is concentrated in telecommunications: 26 of his 31 AI filings name wireless carriers or their trade association.

The client list is CTIA at 10 filings, Lumen at 8, Verizon at 4, AT&T at 4, IAC at 4, and Match Group at 1. That is a telecom and internet-infrastructure portfolio, not a general technology one. The bills attached to his filings, 14 in total, are the legislative surface those clients are tracking.

For AI specifically, this matters because carriers and their trade association are the parties negotiating the physical layer AI depends on: fiber, data centers, and the power and siting rules that govern them. Lobbying on AI bills by telecom clients is one of the few public traces of how that buildout is being shaped before it reaches a permitting docket.

The data does not say what position any client took, what any bill would do, or whether the filings concern AI compute, AI governance, or something else labeled AI. It records that a filing names AI, a lobbyist, a client, and a bill. Nothing here supports a conclusion about influence, and the page states no conclusion about the person.
